title: Evolved stress signalling acts paracrine rather than autocrine

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolved stress signalling acts paracrine rather than autocrine

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy from a cell's stress to its neighbours' states is much larger than to its own state, suggesting that the key signalling mode of stress is paracrine, not autocrine.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We also compared the transfer entropy from stress of one cell to its own state and found it to be much less important than the transfer entropy from the stress of one cell to the states of its neighbours (figure 8c). This suggests the key signalling mode for the stress is paracrine, not autocrine.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-09: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.91

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The exact time series can be regenerated and the two transfer-entropy quantities recomputed from public code. Functional ablations can further discriminate paracrine from autocrine importance within the model.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate cell-level stress and state time series, compute transfer entropy from stress to the same cell and to neighboring cells under identical estimators, and compare magnitudes with uncertainty. Targeted neighbor-link ablations can test whether the larger paracrine flow is functionally important.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Transfer entropy estimates depend on discretization and history length.

Information flow does not by itself establish causal signalling function.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.97
data existence: 0.98
analysis feasibility: 0.82
discriminating power: 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Paracrine versus autocrine use is operationalized as a comparison of two transfer entropies, which is a standard calculation on simulation logs. Those logs and a complete analysis configuration are not in the public snapshot, so the comparison requires regenerating tissues first. The test is well posed and only partly feasible with what was released.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On the original unperturbed runs, compute transfer entropy from each cell's stress to its own next state and to its neighbours' states. A substantially larger neighbour term would support paracrine dominance; a larger self term would support autocrine dominance and refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Transfer entropy depends on binning, history length and which evolved tissue is logged.

The analysis script expects a general parameter file that is not in the repository, and the trajectories are not archived.
